title: Conditional Statements and Proof
seo_title: Conditional Statements Worksheet: Converse, Inverse, Contrapositive (Geometry) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on conditional statements: converse, inverse, contrapositive, counterexamples, laws of logic and reasons in proofs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: If p, then q. The contrapositive (if not q, then not p) is true exactly when the original is.
key_sub: A converse can be false even when the statement is true. One counterexample disproves a statement.
body_html:
How it works

A conditional statement has the form If p, then q. p is the hypothesis and q is the conclusion.

  • Converse: If q, then p (switch).
  • Inverse: If not p, then not q (negate).
  • Contrapositive: If not q, then not p (switch and negate). It always has the same truth value as the original.

One counterexample (hypothesis true, conclusion false) proves a statement false.

In a proof, every step needs a reason: a given fact, a definition, a postulate, a theorem, or a property such as the Transitive Property.

Example

Write the contrapositive of "If two angles are vertical angles, then they are congruent."

Switch the parts and negate both

Answer: If two angles are not congruent, then they are not vertical angles. (True)

Example

If it rains, the game is canceled. If the game is canceled, we go to the movies. It rains. What happens?

Law of Syllogism: if it rains, we go to the movies

Law of Detachment: it rains, so we go to the movies

Answer: We go to the movies.

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the converse and the inverse. Converse switches; inverse negates.
  • Assuming the converse of a true statement is true. Vertical angles are congruent, but congruent angles are not always vertical.
  • Reasoning backward. If p then q, and q is true, tells you nothing about p.
  • Mixing up symmetric (a = b, so b = a) and transitive (a = b and b = c, so a = c).

faq.q: What is the contrapositive of a conditional statement?
faq.a: Switch the hypothesis and conclusion and negate both: if not q, then not p. It is true exactly when the original statement is true.
An example where the hypothesis is true but the conclusion is false. One counterexample is enough to show a statement is false.

faq.q: What is the Law of Detachment?
faq.a: If 'if p, then q' is true and p is true, then q is true.

faq.q: What is the Law of Syllogism?
faq.a: If 'if p, then q' and 'if q, then r' are both true, then 'if p, then r' is true.
